newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares shrug off U.S. data to break records.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares shrug off U.S. data to break records.

text.p: Danish shares cocked a snoot at U.S. price data and German budget worries to close Thursday at record highs for the third consecutive day.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.15 point up from Wednesday's close -- a 1.19 percent gain -- at 165.85. Its June future was up 1.85 point, at 165.00.
The charge was led by shipping group A.P.Moeller. The Moeller group's D/S Svendborg B share was up 9,333 crowns, to 329,333 and D/S 1912 B was up 7,000 crowns to 234,000.
Dealers said they were pushed up by a knock-on effect after better-than-expected first quarter results from Norwegian shipping heavyweight Bergesen, compounded by a lack of Moeller shares for sale.

Novo Nordisk, which on Wednesday reported better than expected first quarter earnings, also performed well, rising 15 crowns to a new year-high of 718.00 --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 3396950
